queue.outcome: openspec/changes/2026-08-27-work-is-isolated-per-task/ - proposal.md, design.md (D1-D7, each with rejected alternatives), tasks.md (8 phases, 55 tasks, tests first), and six spec deltas: MODIFIED operator-agent-creation/'Operator-created agents preserve runtime isolation', agent-context-onboarding/'An agent is told where it is working', agent-configuration/'An agent's workspace states where it works...', task-lifecycle-governance/'Approval integrates the approved work'; ADDED operator-agent-creation/'Work already under way keeps the checkout it started in', run-task-binding/'A turn's task is resolved before its workspace is chosen', task-dependencies/'A task's checkout carries the work it depends on', task-lifecycle-governance/'A finished task's checkout is released, and its branch is not'. `npx openspec validate --all --strict` = 42 passed / 0 failed. DECISIONS R2/R3 MUST CHECK, NOT RE-TAKE: (D1) task worktree is cut from Project.main_branch else HEAD, then each DIRECT prerequisite's accepted evidence commit is merged; a conflict refuses the turn all-or-nothing. Making the dependency gate require *integrated* was REFUSED because NOTHING_TO_MERGE fires for every paths-footprint project (task_integration.py:150 calls that a supported shape), which would leave such a project permanently unable to advance a chain. (D2) resolve_bound_task moves from agent_trigger.py:558 to just after repo_root at :469 - verified read-only by reading all three of its queries; the one behaviour change is that a bad task id is now refused before a checkout is provisioned. (D3) an unbound turn keeps the per-agent worktree, permanently - the workspace is keyed by what the turn is ABOUT. (D4) grandfather the TASK, not the branch: a task with a prior Run carrying non-null snapshot_commit_sha and no task branch stays per-agent for life; self-extinguishing. ADOPTING the agent branch as the task branch was refused as shipping a knowingly-false guarantee. (D5) release on either terminal status, after integrate_task, branch always kept. (D6) branches are agentweave/task/<task_id> and checkouts .agentweave/tasks/<task_id> - the `task/` segment is LOAD-BEARING because task ids match _AGENT_NAME_RE. (D7) Run gains a column recording the workspace it ran in; footprint_root reads it, because every derivation is wrong for a review run. THREE THINGS R1 FOUND THE EXPLORATION HAD NOT: inverting test_rode_along_commits_names_what_actually_landed needs a FIXTURE change (both fixtures build the agent branch by hand and never touch provisioning, so a flipped assertion is red against every implementation); list_agent_branches would silently drop task branches and make GET /worktrees/conflicts return [] forever; and the exploration's guess at the affected capabilities was wrong - the isolation guarantee lives in operator-agent-creation, which was not on its list. Four of 57 file:line citations were wrong and were corrected mechanically before commit.

NEW, measured 2026-08-27 (iteration 6): a test that mocks `PtySession.spawn` with a SHARED session object (`MagicMock(return_value=_completed_session(...))`) can hang the whole pytest process forever, not just fail, if a second real turn for the same agent reuses that same mock. `agent_trigger.py`'s own turn-completion path calls `schedule_agent` again UNCONDITIONALLY whenever a turn ends with entries still queued ('a turn ending with queued entries starts the next turn without waiting for operator input') - this is not something a test opts into, it fires for every job/flow-fired queue with more than one entry. If the second spawn reuses an already-exhausted `read.side_effect` list, the 3rd `pty.read()` call raises `StopIteration`, and `asyncio.Future.set_exception` explicitly refuses to accept `StopIteration` (a PEP-479-era guard) - so `run_in_executor`'s own exception-reporting callback raises, the future is never resolved, and `await` on it hangs with the event loop sitting idle (near-zero CPU, easy to mistake for 'still working'). Always give `spawn` a `side_effect` that produces a FRESH session object per call (e.g. a lambda) when a test's agent has more than one queued entry, even if the test only intends to observe the first turn - self-continuation may still spawn a second one inside the same `_drain()`. To localise a hang like this: `faulthandler`'s thread-dump only shows 'sitting in the event loop', not useful; instead schedule a diagnostic `asyncio.create_task` that sleeps a few seconds then calls `t.print_stack()` on every `asyncio.all_tasks()` - that shows the actual awaited coroutine chain.

method_reminders: THE OPERATOR'S ROUND DISCIPLINE - restated by the operator on 2026-08-27 ("Dont forget the explain/propose review review pattern") and BINDING on every change in this queue. They also said of it: "Take not of this pattern I liked a lot." A change with NO artifacts yet gets THREE rounds before ANY implementation: (R1) explore the codebase, THEN propose - proposal.md, design.md with rejected alternatives, tasks.md, and spec deltas; (R2) an independent pass that compares the change AGAINST THE CODE, claim by claim, and FIXES the artifacts; (R3) a second independent pass doing the same, for what R2 missed. Only then IMPL. A change that is ALREADY proposed gets ONE verification round instead of three. Do not collapse the rounds to save time - the cost IS the point. WHY: this repository's dominant failure mode is a fix that passes its tests and cannot fire in production, and a proposal that reads plausibly but does not match the code produces exactly that. The discipline earned its cost on its first outing (2026-08-27): R2 of reachable-by-a-human found push_log broadcasting raw severity to SSE independently of the normalisation, which R1's proposal had missed entirely.
Use the real surface. Never simulate a step. If something has no API, that absence IS the finding - write it down and continue. This is how 'no integration step exists' surfaced.
Play the operator honestly, and leave something unanswered. A tester who answers everything never discovers which questions silently evaporate.

Watch the seams: between exploring and proposing, between an approved document and a task, between a completed task and a reviewed one, between one agent and the next. The defects are there, not inside a phase.
Read what the agent actually said. The transcript is evidence. Do not dismiss an agent's account of its own failure - verify it.
Follow peer-triggered work, not just what you triggered. Runs an agent starts by messaging another take a different path through the code, and that is where posture and continuity get lost.

Never accept 'the tests pass' as evidence. Run them yourself, then recompute a result by hand and compare. Check the rows, not the chat: an agent's summary of what it did is a claim, the rows are the fact.
A green suite agrees with broken behaviour more often than you expect. Mutation-check anything you claim: delete the line the test exists for, and watch a NAMED test fail.
The best evidence is the failure you did not stage. Watch for unprovoked failures and write them up when they happen.
Say when you contaminated your own test. Testing code you wrote yourself inherits your blind spots - a finding you did NOT make is weaker evidence, and the operator needs to know which is which.
Record what HELD, not only what broke. A gate that correctly refused something is a result the next session needs.
